issues.title: Chunked upload resume
issues.description:
Uploads above 2 GB restart from zero whenever the connection drops. The ingest API already stores completed chunks; the client just never asks what it can skip.

Epic scope: resumable uploads end to end — chunk manifest endpoint, client resume logic, and a progress UI that survives a page reload.

issues.title: Ingest API: expose the chunk manifest for an in-flight upload
issues.description:
`GET /uploads/{id}/chunks` should list the chunk indexes already persisted so a client can resume.

Done when: endpoint returns the persisted chunk set, is covered by an integration test, and is documented in the OpenAPI schema.

comments.body: Landed behind the `resumable_uploads` flag. Chunk set is returned as ranges, not a raw index list — a 40 GB upload has ~20k chunks and the list form was 300 KB of JSON.

issues.title: Web uploader: resume from the chunk manifest instead of restarting
issues.description: On reconnect the uploader should fetch the manifest and skip persisted chunks. Progress bar must reflect skipped chunks immediately rather than racing to 99% and stalling.

comments.body: Resume works; the stall at 99% turned out to be the checksum pass on the final chunk running on the main thread. Moving it to a worker.
Can we surface "verifying…" as its own state? Users read a frozen bar as a failed upload and hit cancel, which is what actually loses the upload.

issues.title: Search returns deleted assets for saved filters
issues.description:
Steps: delete an asset, open any saved filter that matched it. The asset still appears until the nightly reindex.

Expected: delete should enqueue an index removal, same as create/update already do. The saved-filter cache also needs invalidating — it holds result ids for 15 minutes.

comments.body: Regression from the 2026.30 indexer refactor: the delete consumer was renamed and the queue binding kept the old name, so deletes have been dead-lettering for two weeks. Draining the DLQ reindexes ~40k documents.
DLQ drained on staging, counts match. Adding an alert on dead-letter depth so a silent binding break can't run for two weeks again.

issues.title: Transcode farm: H.265 jobs time out on 4K sources over 90 minutes
issues.description:
Long 4K sources hit the 90-minute per-job ceiling and get requeued forever — the third retry lands on the same ceiling. Split long sources into segment jobs and stitch, or raise the ceiling per-preset.

Decision needed: segmenting changes output GOP alignment; stitching must be frame-accurate.

comments.body: Went with per-preset ceilings as the stopgap (H.265/4K gets 4h) while the segmented pipeline is designed properly. Segmenting is the right end state but not a hotfix.

issues.title: Mobile app logs out every user when the token refresh races
issues.description:
Two parallel API calls both notice the access token expired and both redeem the refresh token; the second redemption fails and the app treats it as a revoked session.

Fix: single-flight the refresh in the API client. Server side is already idempotent within a 10 s grace window — the client just doesn't use it.

comments.body: Single-flight mutex shipped in mobile-3.14.2. Logout reports dropped from ~120/day to zero over the weekend.

issues.title: Bulk tagging
issues.description: Selecting 500 assets and adding a tag issues 500 sequential PATCH calls — three minutes of spinner. Epic: one bulk endpoint, optimistic UI, and audit entries that record the batch as one action rather than 500.

issues.title: API: POST /assets/bulk with per-item results
issues.description: Accept up to 1000 asset ids + a patch document. Response is per-item status so a partial failure doesn't hide which items missed. Rate-limit as ONE call.

issues.title: Audit log: batch entries collapse into one row with an expandable detail
issues.description: A 500-asset bulk tag today would write 500 audit rows and make the log unreadable. Batch writes should produce one row ("tagged 500 assets: +archive") expandable to the item list.

issues.title: Thumbnails render magenta for ProRes 4444 sources with alpha
issues.description:
The thumbnailer maps the alpha channel onto the second chroma plane for 4444 sources — output is uniformly magenta. Repro: any ProRes 4444 file with alpha, 100% of the time.

Suspect the pixel-format negotiation in the extract step; 4444 without alpha is fine.

comments.body: Confirmed: the extractor requests yuv444p for anything reporting 4:4:4 and silently drops the alpha-aware variant. One-line format map fix plus a golden-image test with an alpha source.

issues.title: Share links: expiry picker offers dates in the past
issues.description: The date picker allows selecting yesterday; the API correctly 422s, so the user gets a form error after the fact. Disable past dates client-side and default to +7 days.

issues.title: Ingest rejects files with uppercase extensions
issues.description: `.MOV` and `.WAV` are refused with "unsupported container" while `.mov`/`.wav` work. The allowlist compare is case-sensitive. Two-line fix; add a test with a mixed-case fixture name.

comments.body: This also fixed the camera-card imports from the field kits — those always come in uppercase. Support had three open tickets pointing at the same cause.

issues.title: Search: prefix queries under three characters return nothing instead of a hint
issues.description: Typing "ab" shows an empty result panel — looks like there are no matches, actually the server refuses sub-3-char prefixes. Show "keep typing…" instead of an empty state.

issues.title: Nightly backup verification job has been silently skipped since the runner image bump
issues.description:
The verification stage needs `pg_restore` in the runner image; the slim image bump dropped it. The job "passes" because the stage is `allow_failure: true` — so we have unverified backups for 11 days.

Restore the tool, make the stage blocking, and alert on skip.

comments.body: Verified the last 11 nightly artifacts by hand after the fix — all restore clean. The allow_failure flag is gone; a missing tool now fails the pipeline loudly.
Wrote up the lesson in the runbook: a verification that can be skipped is not a verification. Same pattern audit found two more allow_failure stages worth revisiting.

issues.title: Slow asset grid: virtualize rows past 1,000 results
issues.description: The grid renders every result row; at 5k results, scroll jank makes the page unusable (~4 s long tasks on a mid-range laptop). Virtualize with a fixed row height and keep selection state outside the DOM.

issues.title: Webhook deliveries: retry with backoff and a dead-letter view
issues.description: A consumer that 500s three times currently loses the delivery. Add exponential backoff (max 6 attempts over ~2 h) and a per-endpoint dead-letter list with manual replay.

issues.title: Proxy playback stutters on Windows + hybrid GPUs
issues.description: Reports cluster on laptops with integrated+discrete GPUs: the player negotiates hardware decode on the iGPU while the browser composites on the dGPU, and every frame crosses adapters. Force software decode as a user-visible fallback toggle until the heuristic is right.

issues.title: SSO group sync drops users whose directory group list exceeds one page
issues.description: The group-claim fetch reads only the first page of the directory response; a user in 200+ groups loses membership-mapped roles on next login. Page through the overage endpoint like the spec says.

comments.body: Repro'd with a synthetic directory user in 250 groups. Fix pages the overage endpoint and caches the resolved set for the session; adds a regression test at the page boundary (199/200/201).

issues.title: Storage usage report
issues.description: Finance asks monthly for per-team storage. Epic: nightly rollup per team/project, a report page with a trend chart, and CSV export. No live scanning — the rollup is the read model.

issues.title: Nightly per-team storage rollup job
issues.description: Sum object sizes per team/project into a `storage_rollups` table keyed by day. Backfill 12 months from bucket inventory on first run.

issues.title: Report page: storage trend per team with CSV export
issues.description: Line chart over the rollup table, team picker, month range, one-click CSV of the visible series.

issues.title: Comment mentions fire an email even when the mentioned user is the author
issues.description: Writing "as @maya said…" in your own comment emails you about your own comment. Suppress self-mentions at the notification fan-out, not in the editor.

issues.title: Ingest watchdog restarts healthy workers under sustained load
issues.description:
The liveness probe times out when a worker is mid-checksum on a large file — the worker is healthy, just busy. Probe should check the heartbeat file, not make an HTTP call the busy loop can't answer.

Evidence: 61 restarts across the fleet on Monday's 8 TB delivery, zero failed jobs — every restart was a false positive that re-queued work.

comments.body: Heartbeat-file probe on staging since Tuesday: zero false restarts through two synthetic 10 TB deliveries. Rolling to production behind the next release.

issues.title: Trash: assets restore into the wrong folder when the original was moved after deletion
issues.description: Restore uses the folder id captured at delete time; if the folder was since moved, the asset reappears in the folder's OLD location as rendered by the stale breadcrumb cache. Data is fine, presentation is wrong — refresh fixes it. Invalidate the breadcrumb cache on restore.

issues.title: API rate limit responses missing Retry-After
issues.description: 429s carry no Retry-After header, so well-behaved clients guess. The limiter already knows the window reset; put it on the wire and document it.

issues.title: Weekly digest email renders raw markdown in Outlook
issues.description: The digest template ships markdown bullets straight into the HTML body; every client that doesn't auto-render markdown (Outlook desktop, mostly) shows literal asterisks. Render server-side like the notification mails already do.

comments.body: Same renderer the notification mailer uses is importable as-is; the digest predates it and was never migrated. One template swap plus a snapshot test.
